points.title: 犹太教育时期
points.description: 斯宾诺莎出生于阿姆斯特丹的一个葡萄牙裔犹太商人家庭。在犹太拉比的指导下接受了传统的犹太教育，学习了希伯来文、圣经和塔木德。然而，他同时接触了笛卡尔的哲学和科学思想，这与他接受的宗教教育产生了冲突。这一时期，他开始质疑传统宗教教条，并形成了自己的哲学思考。1650年左右，他开始与一些怀疑论者和自由思想家交往，这进一步加深了他对传统宗教的质疑。
points.descriptionEn: Spinoza was born in Amsterdam to a family of Portuguese Jewish merchants. Under the guidance of Jewish rabbis, he received traditional Jewish education, learning Hebrew, the Bible, and Talmud. However, he simultaneously encountered Cartesian philosophy and scientific ideas, which conflicted with his religious education. During this period, he began to question traditional religious doctrines and form his own philosophical thoughts. Around 1650, he started associating with skeptics and free thinkers, which further deepened his doubts about traditional religion.

points.title: 思想转变期
points.description: 这一时期，斯宾诺莎的思想发生了重大转变。他开始系统研究笛卡尔、霍布斯等哲学家的著作，同时对圣经进行批判性解读。他质疑圣经的神圣性和启示的真实性，认为许多故事是寓言性的而非字面真实的。1656年，他因质疑犹太教义和被怀疑无神论而被犹太社区革除教籍（cherem），这是当时最严厉的宗教惩罚。这一事件彻底改变了斯宾诺莎的人生轨迹，迫使他离开犹太社区，开始独立生活和思考。
points.descriptionEn: During this period, Spinoza underwent a significant intellectual transformation. He began systematically studying the works of philosophers like Descartes and Hobbes, while critically interpreting the Bible. He questioned the sacredness of the Bible and the authenticity of revelation, arguing that many stories were allegorical rather than literally true. In 1656, he was excommunicated (cherem) from the Jewish community for questioning Jewish doctrines and suspected atheism, the most severe religious punishment of the time. This event completely changed Spinoza's life trajectory, forcing him to leave the Jewish community and begin independent living and thinking.

points.title: 隐居与著述初期
points.description: 被犹太社区驱逐后，斯宾诺莎搬到莱顿附近的一个乡村，以磨制镜片为生，同时开始系统撰写他的哲学著作。这一时期，他完成了《神学政治论》（Tractatus Theologico-Politicus）的初稿，这是一部大胆的著作，批判了圣经的神圣性，主张宗教宽容和思想自由。他还开始发展自己的形而上学体系，提出了著名的实体一元论。尽管生活简朴，但斯宾诺莎的思想逐渐吸引了少数追随者，包括一些重要的知识分子。这一时期的生活虽然孤独，但却是他思想形成的关键阶段。
points.descriptionEn: After being expelled from the Jewish community, Spinoza moved to the countryside near Leiden, making a living by grinding lenses while beginning to systematically write his philosophical works. During this period, he completed the first draft of the Tractatus Theologico-Politicus, a bold work that criticized the sacredness of the Bible and advocated for religious tolerance and freedom of thought. He also began developing his own metaphysical system, proposing his famous substance monism. Despite his simple life, Spinoza's ideas gradually attracted a small following, including some important intellectuals. This period, though lonely, was crucial for the formation of his thought.

points.title: 哲学体系构建期
points.description: 1660年左右，斯宾诺莎搬到海牙，继续以磨制镜片为生，同时专注于哲学研究。这一时期，他完成了《伦理学》（Ethica）的主要部分，这部著作系统地阐述了他的哲学体系，包括实体、上帝、自然和自由等核心概念。他提出了著名的'上帝即自然'（Deus sive Natura）的观点，认为上帝与自然是一体的，反对传统的人格化上帝观念。斯宾诺莎还与当时的一些重要知识分子保持联系，包括莱布尼茨，尽管他们最终在哲学观点上存在分歧。这一时期，他的思想逐渐成熟，为后世留下了重要的哲学遗产。
points.descriptionEn: Around 1660, Spinoza moved to The Hague, continuing to make a living by grinding lenses while focusing on philosophical research. During this period, he completed most of his Ethica, systematically expounding his philosophical system, including core concepts such as substance, God, nature, and freedom. He proposed his famous 'God or Nature' (Deus sive Natura) view, arguing that God and nature are one, opposing the traditional anthropomorphic concept of God. Spinoza also maintained contact with some important intellectuals of the time, including Leibniz, though they ultimately disagreed on philosophical points. During this period, his thought gradually matured, leaving an important philosophical legacy for later generations.

points.title: 晚年与遗著整理
points.description: 斯宾诺莎的晚年生活相对平静，他继续完善自己的哲学著作，同时开始研究政治哲学和伦理学。1670年，他匿名出版了《神学政治论》，这部著作因其激进的思想在当时引起了巨大争议。斯宾诺莎的健康状况逐渐恶化，可能是因为长期接触玻璃粉尘导致的肺部疾病。1677年，斯宾诺莎在海牙去世，年仅44岁。去世后，他的朋友整理并出版了他的遗著，包括《伦理学》、《政治论》和《知性改进论》等，这些著作对后世哲学产生了深远影响。斯宾诺莎的思想虽然在他生前受到压制，但后来成为启蒙运动的重要思想资源。
points.descriptionEn: Spinoza's later years were relatively peaceful. He continued to refine his philosophical works while beginning to study political philosophy and ethics. In 1670, he anonymously published the Tractatus Theologico-Politicus, which caused great controversy at the time due to its radical ideas. Spinoza's health gradually deteriorated, possibly due to lung disease from long-term exposure to glass dust. In 1677, Spinoza died in The Hague at the age of 44. After his death, his friends整理并出版了他的遗著，包括《伦理学》、《政治论》和《知性改进论》等，这些著作对后世哲学产生了深远影响。斯宾诺莎的思想虽然在他生前受到压制，但后来成为启蒙运动的重要思想资源。

appraisal.zh: 斯宾诺莎通常被视为理性主义的伟大先驱和现代思想的奠基人之一，其实体一元论与泛神论为科学理性与思想自由提供了哲学基础，对启蒙运动影响深远。不过也有研究者指出，他的学说曾被指为无神论，决定论被质疑否定自由意志与道德责任，政治思想也被认为过于理想化、缺乏经验根基。总体而言，他被看作跨越时代的思想革新者，生前虽受压制，其影响却延续至后世众多思想家。
appraisal.en: Spinoza is generally regarded as a great pioneer of rationalism and a founder of modern thought, whose substance monism and pantheism gave philosophical grounding to scientific reason and freedom of thought and deeply influenced the Enlightenment. Yet some researchers note that his teaching was accused of atheism, that his determinism was said to deny free will and moral responsibility, and that his political thought seemed too idealistic and lacking empirical footing. On the whole he is seen as a thinker ahead of his time, suppressed in life but influential on later generations.

supporter.zh: 斯宾诺莎被视为理性主义哲学的伟大先驱和现代思想的奠基人之一。他的实体一元论和泛神论思想打破了传统宗教的束缚，为科学理性和思想自由提供了哲学基础。他强调理性、自由和道德自主，对启蒙运动产生了深远影响。支持者认为，斯宾诺莎的哲学体系代表了人类理性思考的巅峰，他的伦理学思想为现代世俗道德观奠定了基础，他的政治哲学则为民主和宽容提供了理论支持。
supporter.en: Spinoza is regarded as a great pioneer of rationalist philosophy and one of the founders of modern thought. His substance monism and pantheistic ideas broke free from traditional religious constraints, providing a philosophical foundation for scientific reason and freedom of thought. He emphasized reason, freedom, and moral autonomy, profoundly influencing the Enlightenment. Supporters believe that Spinoza's philosophical system represents the pinnacle of human rational thinking, his ethical ideas laid the foundation for modern secular morality, and his political philosophy provided theoretical support for democracy and tolerance.

critic.zh: 批评者认为斯宾诺莎的哲学存在严重缺陷。首先，他的泛神论被指责为无神论，否认了人格化的上帝和宗教的启示意义。其次，他的决定论观点被认为否定了人的自由意志和道德责任。此外，他的政治思想被认为过于理想化，忽视了人性的复杂性和现实政治的困境。批评者还指出，斯宾诺莎的哲学体系虽然逻辑严密，但缺乏经验基础，过于抽象和形而上，难以指导实际生活。
critic.en: Critics argue that Spinoza's philosophy has serious flaws. First, his pantheism was accused of atheism, denying the personal God and the revelatory significance of religion. Second, his deterministic view is seen as negating human free will and moral responsibility. Additionally, his political thought is considered too idealistic, overlooking the complexity of human nature and the dilemmas of real politics. Critics also point out that while Spinoza's philosophical system is logically rigorous, it lacks empirical foundation, being too abstract and metaphysical to guide practical life.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，斯宾诺莎被定义为一位跨越时代的思想革新者。他的思想虽然在他生前受到压制，但对后世产生了深远影响。他被视为启蒙运动的重要先驱，影响了从莱布尼茨到黑格尔再到爱因斯坦等众多思想家。在流行文化中，斯宾诺莎常被描绘为孤独的思想者，为真理而牺牲世俗生活的典范。他的哲学思想在当代依然具有现实意义，特别是在科学与宗教关系、自由意志与决定论等议题上提供了独特的视角。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Spinoza is defined as a revolutionary thinker who transcended his time. Although his ideas were suppressed during his lifetime, they had a profound impact on later generations. He is regarded as an important precursor to the Enlightenment, influencing many thinkers from Leibniz to Hegel to Einstein. In popular culture, Spinoza is often depicted as a lonely thinker who sacrificed worldly life for truth. His philosophical ideas remain relevant today, offering unique perspectives on issues such as the relationship between science and religion, free will and determinism.

self.zh: 自由不在于随心所欲，而在于自我主宰。
self.en: Freedom is not the power of doing what we will, but the necessity of doing what we ought.
